html:
The Battle of Culloden was fought on 16 April 1746 on Culloden Moor, near Inverness in the Scottish Highlands. A British government army under the Duke of Cumberland crushed the Jacobite army of Charles Edward Stuart, known as Bonnie Prince Charlie. It was the last pitched battle fought in Britain.

The Jacobites wanted to put the Stuart family back on the British throne, which it had lost in 1688. With promises of help from France, Charles landed in Scotland in 1745, raised an army mostly of Highland clans, took Edinburgh and marched into England as far as Derby, then turned back. At Culloden his tired and hungry men, about 6,000, faced about 8,000 well-fed soldiers with cannon. The Highland charge crossed boggy ground under heavy fire and broke on the bayonets. The battle lasted under an hour. Between 1,500 and 2,000 Jacobites were killed or wounded, against about 300 on the government side.

Cumberland's men killed many of the wounded. Charles escaped to France. New laws disarmed the Highlands, banned Highland dress and took away the chiefs' powers, which broke the clan system. The Jacobite cause was finished, and the rule of the Hanoverian kings over Britain was safe.
